title: Design an API Rate Limiting Service
summary: Design a centralized rate limiting service for a microservices architecture.
body:
Design a centralized rate limiting service for a microservices architecture.

## Scenario

Design a rate limiting service that multiple backend services can use to enforce per-user and per-API rate limits.

## Requirements

- Support multiple rate limiting algorithms (fixed window, sliding window, token bucket)
- Per-user, per-API, and global rate limits
- Sub-millisecond decision latency
- Dashboard for monitoring and configuration
- Graceful degradation when rate limiter is unavailable

## Constraints

- Must handle 1M+ decisions per second
- Decision latency < 1ms at p99
- No false negatives (never allow over-limit requests)
- Minimal false positives (< 0.1% wrongly rejected)

## What a strong answer covers

- Choice of data store (Redis, in-memory)
- Synchronization strategy across instances
- Rule configuration and hot-reload
- Client library design
- Failure mode design

## Reference walkthrough

Redis-backed with Lua scripts for atomic operations. Sliding window counter as default algorithm. Client library with local token bucket as first-line defense, Redis check as second line. Rules stored in Redis with pub/sub for hot reload. If Redis unavailable, fall back to local rate limiting with conservative limits. Return rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-*) for client visibility.
